current: `fahren mit + Dat` — `Ich fahre mit dem Zug.`
correct: Remove from the fixed verb–preposition bank; teach `mit + Dat` separately as transport/means (and accompaniment).

current: `gründen auf + Akk` — `be based on / found on` — `Die Theorie gründet auf Fakten.`
correct: For the intransitive illustrated sense use `gründen auf + Dat`, preferably with an unambiguous example such as `Die Theorie gründet auf einer falschen Annahme.` Reserve `auf + Akk` for transitive `etwas auf etwas gründen`.
why: Intransitive `etwas gründet auf etwas` meaning “is based on” takes dative; plural `Fakten` hides the incorrect case label.

current: `kommen zu + Dat` — `come to / arrive at` — `Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?`
correct: Remove this literal destination use from the fixed-government bank, or replace it with a genuinely lexical pattern such as `zu einem Ergebnis kommen` and a matching gloss/example.
why: `zum Bahnhof` is an ordinary destination phrase; the destination determines whether German uses `zu`, `nach`, `in`, etc., not fixed government of `kommen`.

current: `tun für + Akk` — `Was kann ich für Sie tun?`
correct: Remove from the fixed verb–preposition bank.
why: `für Sie` is an ordinary beneficiary phrase that can accompany innumerable verbs, not a prepositional object fixed by `tun`.

current: `blicken auf + Akk` — `look at / look back on` — `Er blickt auf eine lange Karriere zurück.`
correct: Either use `blicken auf` only for literal `look at` with a matching example, or change the headword to `zurückblicken auf`; the latter already occurs later in this batch.
why: `blickt ... zurück` is the separated form of `zurückblicken`, not an example of plain `blicken`; the current row conflates two verbs and duplicates the later construction.

current: `sich freisprechen von + Dat` — `Das Gericht spricht ihn vom Vorwurf frei.`
correct: `jemanden von etwas freisprechen` / headword `freisprechen von + Dat`
why: In the acquittal sense, `freisprechen` is transitive, not reflexive; the example itself correctly contains `ihn`, not `sich`.

current: `bieten an + Akk` — `offer (to someone)` — `Er bietet die Ware an.`
correct: Remove this row from the fixed-government bank and teach the separable verb `anbieten` in the ordinary verb bank.
why: In `bietet ... an`, `an` is the separated prefix of `anbieten`; there is no `an + Akk` prepositional phrase at all.

current: `gelangen in + Akk` — `get into / reach` — `Die Daten gelangen in das System.`
correct: Remove this literal destination use from the fixed-government bank, or restrict the row to a clearly lexical construction and label it accordingly.
why: `in das System` is a directional destination phrase; `gelangen` also combines with destination-dependent `zu`, `nach`, `auf`, etc., so `in` is not fixed government here.

current: `zurückkehren nach + Dat` — `return to` — `Sie kehrt nach Wien zurück.`
correct: Remove from the fixed-government bank and teach destination prepositions as a separate rule.
why: `nach Wien` is an ordinary destination construction (contrast `in die Schweiz`, `zum Bahnhof`); `nach` is chosen by the kind of place name, not governed by `zurückkehren`.
